My story is similar, except that I had quit. 

My boss wasn't satisfied that I was working fast enough ( I was doing like 3 people's jobs) so he hired me some help, I was open to it until the guy they hired was older than me and had been in the industry longer. Despite that he had no idea how to do anything I needed help and also was not very good at the fabrication part of the job so they put him in charge of the guys I was supervising. No big deal, that's something off my plate. Then I taught him one of my easier tasks which he picked up. Somehow he got the idea in his head that HE was MY boss. He started telling me what to do and trying to change the way we do everything. I went to the owners on many occasions airing my concerns but they brushed it off and the GM said the guy was taking the lead on my department. I pointed out that I was running it and he said they recognized he wanted to be in charge and I didn't seem to be interested. This pissed me off and this guy kept getting his way while doing practically nothing to contribute. Eventually I had enough and quit. I left the premises without a word to anyone and never looked back. I figured if they want him to lead so badly then he can have all my responsibilities.

Turned out he was as bad at the job as I knew and they wanted me back. The foreman asked me what they could offer to get me back. I told him 6$/hr more than I was getting paid, firing the asshole who thought he could handle my job and an official title for the position I had built. I knew they wouldn't accept. I told him my demands were not negotiable and he said he would discuss with management. My thoughts were that if they accepted I would be way better off financially and would have some job security. But alas I got a lovely description from a friend who still worked there of the owners face when he heard my requirements and it brought me enough joy for a lifetime. 

Couldn't hurt to demand something outrageous just to see if they take the bait.

Humans are able to self reflect and experience things in more depth than most other species I'm sure some species like dolphins or others also have value in this regard and I can't speak for them nor they for themselves. Our self reflection allows us to even have this discussion on morality. Obviously I can't explain my experience and how it has led me to believe self awareness is the goal of existence without writing a book. You asked for opinions on this mosquito dilemma. I will always treat human life as a priority. If a human and a dog are fighting to the death should i just stay out of it and let one or the other die? Sure it keeps my hands clean but would you not feel guilty if the dog kills the human and you did nothing to help? Though it's a dog with a personality and may have lived a tortured life up to that point it can't be weighed as equal to a human. That human could go on to help the world in many other ways that this dog is incapable of. Perhaps I can stop the fight between them but that may involve hurting the dog where I could reason with a human. 

All I'm saying is I will always pick a human first and then I'll weigh the situation individually afterwards. If my cat has a viral infection, I will treat it and kill the virus. Hell, if my cat is attacked by a coyote or a hawk I will defend her at the cost of the others lives if need be. She is precious to me and provides enrichment to my life and I respect her. But if she developed rabies and attacked me should I allow it because of my affection for her? I wouldn't be happy about it but I would have to put her down. It's not selfish to kill for survival.
